title: Mercedes-Benz Lays Out Supply Chain Decarbonisation Plans
content:
Mercedes-Benz Lays Out Supply Chain Decarbonisation Plans
Prioritise Us
on Google
Mercedes-Benz announces steps to decarbonise its supply chain with First Movers Coalition and Hydro offtake agreement. Credit: Mercedes-Benz
CTO Jörg Burzer at Mercedes-Benz Group introduces plans to lower direct and indirect emissions by 2039, targeting greater green steel and aluminium use
Global automotive giant Mercedes-Benz has officially accelerated its challenging "Ambition 2039" supply chain sustainability strategy. By introducing stringent direct and indirect emission decarbonisation targets and signing a landmark offtake agreement to source up to 10% of its aluminium supply from low-carbon aluminium with Hydro, the enterprise aims to execute a sweeping green digital transformation across its procurement networks, reducing overall carbon footprint across all value chain stages by a targeted 70% by 2039 compared to 2019 levels.
“Aluminium is one of the most important levers in our supply chain. By joining the First Movers Coalition, we are sending a clear signal to the market: we want lower-carbon aluminium in our vehicles. This gives our partners planning security and strengthens the resilience of our supply chain,” comments Jörg Burzer, Member of the Board of Management of Mercedes-Benz Group AG, Chief Technology Officer, Development & Procurement.
Jörg Burzer, Chief Technology Officer at Mercedes-Benz
Expanded aluminium offtake agreement with Hydro
Global automotive giant Mercedes-Benz has significantly expanded its strategic supply chain partnership with Hydro. Mercedes-Benz will source primary aluminium from Hydro from 2026 until beyond 2030, with a contractually defined, step-by-step reduction of its carbon footprint. Under the agreement, Hydro will progressively reduce the carbon footprint of primary aluminium supplied to Mercedes-Benz to 3.5 kg CO2e per kg by 2028 and 3.0 kg CO2e per kg from 2030 onwards. The agreement covers at least 10 percent of Mercedes-Benz’s primary aluminium demand.
The primary aluminium Mercedes-Benz currently sources from Hydro, produced using electrolysis powered by renewable energy, has a footprint of around 4.0 kg CO2e per kg. That is around 72 percent below the global average of 14.4 kg CO2e per kg.
The agreement also covers the introduction of aluminium produced from post-consumer recycled aluminium, Hydro CIRCAL, with use planned from 2027. CIRCAL contains at least 75 percent post-consumer recycled content and has a carbon footprint of no more than 2.0 kg CO2e per kg. In summer 2026, Mercedes-Benz was the first car manufacturer company in Europe to announce the integration of Hydro CIRCAL into series production for the next generation of large electric vehicles from 2027.
Hydro notes that achieving further reductions will require continued technology development and investment. Supply Chain Digital recently
reported
that Hydro had produced its first aluminium from aluminium chloride at at its Herøya research and test facility in Porsgrunn, Norway on 19 October. The technology opens up the prospect of eventually eliminating CO2 emissions from both electrolysis and anode production, releasing oxygen instead of CO2.
A Mercedes-Benz CLA inside the electrolysis hall at Hydro's Årdal smelter in Norway, where renewable energy is used to produce Hydro REDUXA, low-carbon primary aluminium. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro)
Key facts about Mercedes-Benz's Hydro offtake agreement
Hydro will supply at least 10% of Mercedes-Benz’s total primary aluminium demand through this long-term offtake agreement.
Hydro has committed to lowering the carbon footprint of supplied primary aluminium to a maximum of 3.5 kg CO2e per kg by 2028.
Hydro is targeting a further reduction to 3.0 kg CO2e per kg for primary aluminium by 2030.
Hydro will begin to supply Hydro CIRCAL, which utilises a minimum of 75% post-consumer aluminium scrap as feedstock, to Mercedes-Benz in 2027..
Mercedes-Benz announced it was integrating Hydro CIRCAL into series production for the next generation of large electric vehicles from 2027.
Hydrogen-based ironmaking in step towards decarbonising the supply chain
Mercedes-Benz is also seeking to accelerate the introduction of low-emission or green steel produced from a hydrogen-based ironmaking process, after the successful conclusion of a pilot project at HyIron, in which iron ore from Anglo American's Sishen iron ore mine in South Africa was shipped to HyIron's facility before being directly reduced into direct reduced iron (DRI) using hydrogen. By eliminating the energy-intensive pelletisation step, the scope 1 and 2 emissions of the process were lowered to just 10kg per ton of DRI, according to according to HyIron.
During the pilot, the material was then used in steelmaking and formed into a demonstrator component for the Mercedes-Benz EQS. The pilot successfully demonstrated technical feasibility across the value chain. Building on these results, Mercedes-Benz and HyIron have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to advance technical validation towards industrial scale-up and potential next steps.
“In steel, we are building on what we have learned in aluminium: progress happens when partners along the entire value chain work together – from the mine to the finished component. The pilot project with Anglo American and HyIron shows how transparency, responsible sourcing and lower emissions can be considered together. The insights from this pilot will help us decide where such approaches can make a contribution in our steel supply chain,” comments Yanni von Roy-Jiang, Head of Procurement and Supplier Management, Mercedes-Benz AG.
Higher levels of circularity and a lower-carbon footprint can play a role in enhancing the resilience of our automotive supply chains. Together with Hydro, we are making low-carbon aluminium a key pillar in our mass production process.
Yanni von Roy-Jiang, Head of Procurement and Supplier Management at Mercedes-Benz AG
Sharper Sustainability Focus
During the presentation of its detailed CO2 emission reduction strategy at its 'Sustainability Dialogue x Sustainability Update' in Sindelfingen, Mercedes-Benz announced that it was tightening its Sustainability strategy focus around four main pillars.
Decarbonisation: decarbonising the core business along the value chain, with a focus on electrification and on supply chain, logistics and production, in line with Ambition 2039.
Circularity
: expanding the use of recycled materials to 40% within the next decade, in line with Ambition 2039.
Safety: this overarching category now incorporates both traffic safety and digital trust.
People: social responsibility towards employees and respect for human rights across product value chains.
Mercedes-Benz Group is committed to a 90% reduction in production emissions, an 80% cut in use-phase emissions (dependent upon market conditions) , and an overall 70% reduction in CO2 emissions across all relevant value chain stages by 2039 compared to 2019.
Mercedes-Benz plans to target net zero in the course of the following decade. Mercedes-Benz defines net zero as meaning that the CO2 emissions will be reduced by at least 90% compared to 2019.
The Kuppenheim recycling plant is one of the company's strategies of building a circular economy (Kuppenheim recycling plant | Credit: Mercedes-Benz)
Key Partners
Hydro is an aluminium and renewable energy company. Its aluminium operations span the entire value chain, from bauxite mining to finished products. Hydro is an active technology developer researching lower-emission primary aluminium production. Its Herøya Technology Centre in Porsgrunn hosts testing and development of the HalZero process. The programme involves collaboration with Norwegian research institutions including NTNU and SINTEF, while Enova has supported both the test facility and planning for the next development phase.
First Movers Coalition
The First Movers Coalition is a global initiative uniting corporate purchasing power to rapidly commercialise emerging low-carbon technologies. By securing advanced procurement commitments from major multinational enterprises, the coalition accelerates the rapid decarbonisation of hard-to-abate industrial sectors globally.
HyIron has developed a hydrogen-based reduction process for global steelmaking. Its direct reduced iron (DRI) solution offers a solution to reduce emissions from steel supply chains.

title: Vinted Go Expands European Network With Finland Launch
content:
Vinted Go Expands European Network With Finland Launch
Prioritise Us
on Google
Vinted Go is partnering with Unisend as both companies enter the Finnish market. Credit: Vinted Go
Vinted Go is scaling its operations in order to meet consumer demand and grow local businesses, Vytautas Atkočaitis, CEO of Vinted Go, explains
As the recommerce market continues to expand, Vinted Go is launching in Finland.
Vinted’s logistics arm is making it more convenient for Vinted members to buy and sell on the app through a new partnership with Unisend.
Through this, the company is making it more simple for customers to sell their clothes,
preventing fashion from ending up in landfill
Changing consumer patterns
Recommerce – the concept of
selling or renting second-hand
items through online marketplaces – has increased significantly over recent years. Consumers are becoming more economically and environmentally conscious, wanting to save money while still refreshing their wardrobes.
Though charity shops and eBay have been in existence for years, the concentration of these marketplaces have increased. According to OfferUp, 90% of US shoppers bought something second hand in the past 12 months, and 51% of shoppers sold something secondhand in the same period.
As recommerce increases, the need for reliable logistics does too. Recommerce comes with its own challenges – unpredictable volume and condition, case-by-case inspection, value degradation from slow processing.
On C2C sites, such as Vinted, this has extra complexity, as the sellers are non-professionals navigating the market. The logistics challenges of it include fragmented supply chains, vulnerabilities with third-party couriers and high shipping costs relative to item.
Alongside this, many sellers and buyers work, meaning their availability to post or pick up items is limited. As a result, there needs to be some strong last-mile, and first-mile, delivery options. Vinted Go, therefore, is making this process much more streamlined through its partnership with Unisend in Helsinki.
“Second-hand only scales if shipping is effortless and affordable,” explains Vytautas Atkočaitis, CEO of Vinted Go.
Vytautas Atkočaitis, CEO of Vinted Go
“That’s what we’re building: a network that connects members, local businesses and carriers across Europe, offering members accessible, flexible and easy-to-use delivery options. We’re excited to bring that to Finland, starting first in Helsinki, and with plans to go nationwide together with our partner Unisend.”
At a glance
Vinted Go is present in five other European markets
The Helsinki launch includes 300 pick-up and drop-off points
90% of US shoppers bought something second hand in the past 12 months
According to UNEP, the textile industry uses the equivalent of 86 million Olympic-sized swimming pools of water per year
Nearly 40% of consumers surveyed by eBay have sold secondhand items online
Company growth
Unisend, the parcel delivery network operated by Lietuvos paštas, is working with Vinted Go across Finland. The launch has started in the Helsinki area, making use of 300 pick-up and drop-off (PUDO) points.
The PUDO option acts as a more flexible option for many buyers and sellers, particularly when
lockers are used instead of postal stores
. By having accessible reverse logistics infrastructure, businesses meet consumer demand much more effectively.
Lietuvos Paštas is a Lithuanian postal company, operating the LP EXPRESS and Unisend network which consists of 164 post offices and approximately 1,500 parcel machines across Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. Now, it is entering the Finnish market through Unisend’s partnership with Vinted Go.
"Entering the Finnish market marks an important new stage in Unisend's growth,” says Kastytis Valantinas, CEO of Lietuvos paštas.
Kastytis Valantinas, CEO of Lietuvos paštas
“Over more than two years of operations in the Baltic states, we have built a reliable parcel delivery network trusted by both individual and business customers. Our partnership with Vinted Go allows us to bring this experience to a new market and provide Vinted members with a simple and seamless parcel delivery experience.”
At present, Vinted Go has 18,000 PUDO points, with a presence in five other European markets. The company aims to make shipping more flexible, affordable and simpler for people buying and selling second-hand.
In Helsinki, Vinted members are making use of Vinted Go’s 300 PUDO points, based in shops and local spots. They increase convenience and flexibility, as well as increase footfall in local shops.
The partnership is just part of both companies' expansion plans, with potential to grow into more markets in coming years.
Second-hand only scales if shipping is effortless and affordable.
Vytautas Atkočaitis, CEO of Vinted Go
Vinted Go is expanding its operations to Finland. Credit: Getty
Key partners
Vinted is a Lithuanian online marketplace founded in 2008, specializing in secondhand fashion and accessories. The platform enables users to buy, sell, and exchange pre-owned clothing items across Europe and North America. Operating on a peer-to-peer model, Vinted promotes sustainable fashion by extending garment lifecycles. The company generates revenue through buyer protection fees and additional services. With millions of active users, Vinted has become Europe's largest secondhand fashion marketplace, valued at billions.
Lietuvos paštas
Lietuvos paštas (Lithuanian Post) is Lithuania's national postal operator, providing mail delivery, parcel services, and financial services since 1918. As a state-owned enterprise, it maintains an extensive network of post offices throughout Lithuania, serving both urban and rural communities. The company handles domestic and international mail, logistics solutions, and e-commerce deliveries. Lietuvos paštas has modernized its operations to compete in the digital age while maintaining universal postal service obligations to all Lithuanian residents.
ZigZag is a UK-based returns management platform that simplifies the online shopping returns process for consumers and retailers. The service aggregates multiple courier options, allowing customers to return items through convenient drop-off points or collection services. ZigZag partners with retailers to provide branded returns experiences while optimizing logistics and reducing costs. The platform consolidates returns from various carriers, streamlining reverse logistics. ZigZag's technology helps e-commerce businesses improve customer satisfaction while managing the growing challenge of online returns efficiently.
DHL is a German logistics company and the world's leading international express delivery and logistics provider. Founded in 1969, DHL operates in over 220 countries and territories, offering courier, parcel, freight transport, and supply chain management services. As part of Deutsche Post DHL Group, it serves both business and private customers. DHL specializes in international shipping, e-commerce logistics, and time-critical deliveries. The company employs hundreds of thousands worldwide, utilizing air, road, and rail networks to facilitate global trade.

title: Unit1 FARO and NEON review: I just found my new favorite e-bike helmets
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 10 2026 - 7:46 am PT
I test a lot of electric bikes, which means I also spend a lot of time wearing bicycle helmets. And while most helmets tend to fall into the decidedly unexciting category of “necessary safety equipment,” UNIT 1 has managed to make a couple that I actually get excited about wearing.
I’ve been using both the UNIT 1 FARO and the new NEON, and despite taking fairly different approaches, they’ve both become regular go-to helmets for me.
UNIT 1 FARO: High-tech safety with lights everywhere
The FARO is the more futuristic-looking of the two, and it’s also the one that really leans into the “smart helmet” concept.
The helmet includes MIPS protection to reduce rotational impact during a collision, as well as integrated lighting on both the front and rear, including a large customizable rear lighting area made up of dozens of LEDs.
That large rear LED array is a feature I particularly appreciate since visibility is such a major part of cycling safety.
A helmet obviously can’t
drivers to pay attention, but I’d rather give them as many opportunities as possible to see me. The hidden light area below the obvious LED light bar adds a lot of extra visibility.
You can see just how vivid it is in the GIF below, though in real life it looks even better!
The FARO’s lighting system works with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote, which adds turn signals controlled right from the bars.
The system can also provide automatic brake-light functionality, giving you another way to communicate with traffic around you.
I’ll admit that turn signals on bicycles can sometimes feel a bit gimmicky, especially when they’re so close together that drivers can’t really tell which direction is flashing. But putting them high up on the helmet makes them considerably more visible, and the little wireless handlebar remote makes operating them incredibly easy.
The rechargeable lighting is also convenient. I’ve topped up the helmet from a power bank while out and about, meaning you don’t necessarily need to find a wall outlet if you realize your helmet is running low. The rear LED light bar also turns green and illuminates along the length of the bar to let you know what percentage of charge the battery has reached. The only way it could be clearer would be with a screen, but we’re still talking about a helmet here, not a phone.
There are other smart features packed in too, including crash detection and app-based customization.
The tradeoff is weight. At around 640 grams for a medium, the FARO is noticeably heavier than a conventional bicycle helmet. It doesn’t bother me much once I’m riding, and I’ve found the helmet comfortable, but you definitely know there’s more helmet up there. Each time I pick it up, I’m reminded that it’s not just the basic little foam shell that I’ve been wearing for the last few years.
Then there’s the price.
At around $230
(or $195 during the current Black Friday sale period), this isn’t a cheap helmet. You’re paying for all of that technology, lighting, and design.
UNIT 1 NEON: Lighter and perhaps even more practical
As much as I like the FARO, I’ve also become a big fan of the UNIT 1 NEON.
At roughly 430 grams in a medium, it’s significantly lighter than the FARO, and that difference is immediately noticeable. It’s also a bit cheaper at
around $210
(or $178 during the Black Friday sale period) while still packing several of the smart features that make UNIT 1’s helmets interesting.
You still get MIPS rotational protection, crash detection, integrated rear lighting, app connectivity, and compatibility with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote for turn signals and brake-light functionality.
I do wish the NEON had a front light like the FARO. That’s probably the biggest feature I miss when switching between the two. But the NEON makes up for it with one of my favorite features on either helmet: its magnetic face shield.
The shield is ridiculously easy to attach and remove. You don’t even need to carefully line it up. I just need to get it somewhere near the mounting points with one hand and the powerful magnets basically grab it out of the air and snap it into position.
That means I can easily add or remove it one-handed, even while riding.
The photochromic shield is clear enough for night riding but darkens when exposed to bright sunlight, giving you sun protection without requiring separate daytime and nighttime shields. I’ve found that incredibly convenient, especially on rides that transition from daylight into evening. I hate that I can’t wear my sunglasses for eye protection at night, and a lens like this solves that issue.
The NEON also gets something particularly important for faster e-bike riders: NTA 8776 certification. That’s the Dutch standard designed specifically around higher-speed e-bike uses at up to 45 km/h (28 mph). For the Class 3 e-bikes that have become increasingly common in the US, that’s a big distinction compared to helmets rated for crashes at slower speeds.
Which UNIT 1 helmet would I choose?
That’s actually difficult, because I regularly use both.
The FARO is the one I’d choose if maximum visibility and technology were my priorities. I love having LEDs both front and rear, the MIPS protection, and the handlebar-controlled turn signals. It’s comfortable, looks great, and has become one of my favorite urban riding helmets.
But the NEON may be the easier helmet to recommend to most e-bike riders.
It’s lighter, a little cheaper, still gives you a rear light and smart safety features, has that excellent magnetic photochromic face shield, and importantly carries NTA 8776 certification for faster e-bike riding.
Neither helmet is inexpensive, and the FARO in particular asks you to accept some extra weight in exchange for all that technology. But I’m used to wearing much heavier motorcycle helmets and ways.
Plus, it’s important to note that these aren’t helmets I tested for a few rides and then tossed onto a shelf. Both have stayed in my regular rotation, and I find myself reaching for them frequently when I head out on an e-bike. The fact that I not only enjoyed them during my testing but actually replaced my old helmets with them should speak for itself.
For someone who rides as much as I do, that’s probably the strongest endorsement I can give them.
Between solid helmets like these and
safe riding clothing
, it’s good to feel protected!

opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000.
Genesis GV90 prices and driving range in Korea
Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (
which we had the pleasure to see firsthand
), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.
It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.
In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).
Based on Hyundai’s new eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis said the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
A luxury private lounge on wheels
The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.
When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”
The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.
The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its new extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Together, they create what Genesis calls a new realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.
Genesis GV90 Neolun infotainment display (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.
Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.
A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.
In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that shows the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.
The GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.
Meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.
Genesis GV90 debut (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
Dimensions, battery size, other specs
As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).
To power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a big battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis said provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.
The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.
It’s equipped with a new dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.
When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (left) GV90 Neolun First Edition (middle) and GV90 (right) Source: Hyundai
“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a new standard for luxury.”
Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.
Genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.
What do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

title: Lucid says service wait times fell 20% after 40% jump in service staff
content:
Lucid Motors
Lucid Air
Lucid Gravity
Fred Lambert
| Nov 10 2026 - 6:24 am PT
Lucid (LCID) says service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.
The automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.
Lucid hires up service after a year of cuts
Lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its
Q3 2026 earnings
. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.
Lucid’s new combined Studio and Service Center in Mission Viejo, California (Image: Lucid)
The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.
That’s a big hiring push for a company that
laid off 18% of its workforce in June
, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.
And owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.
A Lucid technician at work in a Service Center (Image: Lucid)
Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, said the company is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”
The new Lucid service locations
Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:
Mission Viejo, California:
a new combined Studio and Service Center, open now
Downtown Los Angeles and Dallas:
Studio and Service Center operations later this year
Highland Park, Illinois:
Mobile Service:
20 additional Gravity Mobile Service vehicles in North America
Service bays at Lucid’s Mission Viejo location (Image: Lucid)
Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.
Outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first company-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.
A Lucid Gravity converted for Mobile Service (Image: Lucid)
The numbers Lucid doesn’t give
Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.
A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-issue. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.
It’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid
delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3
, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.
For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.
Electrek’s Take
This is the right move, and it’s overdue.
Lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if
we found its software wasn’t ready
. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.
So growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a big deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.
The problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.

title: Polestar unveils Formula 2030 concept, previewing the next Polestar 2
content:
Polestar
Polestar 2
Polestar 7
Fred Lambert
| Nov 10 2026 - 6:10 am PT
Polestar has now fully unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low four-door electric sports car that previews the design of the next-generation Polestar 2 coming in 2027 and the Polestar 7 compact SUV.
The concept sits just 1,350 mm (53 inches) tall, which is lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer, and it brings physical buttons back into the Swedish brand’s interior.
We reported in September that
Polestar confirmed the Formula 2030 concept
after showing it privately to investors and retailers in Gothenburg. Now we get the full set of pictures and the details.
It’s the first show car built under head of design Philipp Römers, who joined from Audi in 2024.
A low four-door “sports car”
Polestar calls the Formula 2030 a “compact practical four-door sports car” that “sits within its own segment.” It’s 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long and 2,021 mm (79.6 inches) wide, on a 2,780 mm (109.4-inch) wheelbase.
For context, that’s about 3 inches longer than today’s Polestar 2 and roughly 5 inches lower. It’s also a bit shorter than a Tesla Model 3 and sits 3.5 inches closer to the ground. Polestar says the concept lands “somewhere between” the upcoming Polestar 2 and Polestar 7 in size.
The proportions are classic sports car: long hood, short overhangs, the cabin pushed back over big rear haunches, and 22-inch center-lock wheels. There are gold Brembo calipers behind those wheels and Öhlins dampers on display in the trunk.
Up front, Polestar kept its “Dual Blade” headlights, now set into an aero wing over a shark nose and a deep splitter. The automaker says this is the face of the next-generation Polestar 2 planned for 2027.
There’s a single vertical windshield wiper, like on a race car, and a LiDAR unit that hides under an aerodynamic shroud and only shows itself when the car is driving autonomously.
The rear is where things change the most. Polestar dropped the full-width light bar, which is on just about every EV these days, for what it calls “Single Blade” rear lights. It says they are being introduced here “ahead of series production.”
Römers described the concept as a “bold evolution” of the brand’s existing design:
“It is a physical embodiment of how we apply Polestar’s core values of design, performance and sustainability to the next production cars.”
The rear doors are hinged at the back and there’s no B-pillar, so the whole side opens up to four individual seats.
Physical buttons are back
The interior is built around the driver. A curved 20-inch display, which Polestar calls the “HyperDIM,” is mounted directly on the steering column, and a 12.2-inch center screen sits in the center tunnel.
But the bigger news is below that screen. Polestar added a panel of eight physical controls for the most-used functions, and owners could swap between types of controls, like rocker switches or rotary knobs, and program what each one does.
Polestar says it is “committing to rebalance the mix of physical and digital.” Juan Pablo Bernal, the company’s head of interior design, put it plainly:
“As a performance brand, we see a renewed focus on the driver, and so we re-balance the digital and physical. We introduce physical buttons and controls.”
That’s a big change for a brand whose recent cars run almost everything through the center touchscreen.
The cabin also physically changes with the drive mode. There are three of them: Performance, Normal, and Autonomous. In Performance, the center screen drops flush into the console and the steering wheel and its display pull closer to the driver. In Autonomous, the wheel and the seat move away from each other.
The four seats use inflatable bolsters that shape themselves to each occupant, and the seat backs are made of a flax-based composite instead of virgin plastic. Google Gemini is built in, like in Polestar’s production cars.
A see-through trunk floor
The cargo area is the strangest part of the car. The rear opens as a clamshell, and the trunk floor is transparent, with custom Polestar bags strapped down underneath it with gold straps.
Up front, the frunk holds two race helmets and a fire extinguisher, framed by a gold strut brace.
Now for what’s missing. Polestar didn’t release a single powertrain spec. No battery size, no range, no power output, and no price. This is a design study, and Polestar isn’t saying it will build it.
What it does say is that “various design attributes” from the concept will show up on the next Polestar 2 in 2027 and the Polestar 7 in 2028. Those are two of the
four new models Polestar plans to launch in three years
, and the 7 is going to be built in Europe.
Europe is where this matters, since Polestar is
shut out of the US under the federal connected-vehicle rule
. The concept made its debut during the media drive of the
Polestar 4 SUV
Electrek’s Take
Polestar always impresses me with its design, and this is no exception with this new head of design.
The proportions are sharp. Long hood, cabin pushed back, big haunches, and a roofline lower than the Polestar 5’s on a car with four doors and four real seats. If the next Polestar 2 keeps even half of this stance, it’s going to be the best-looking car in its segment.
I don’t know about the trunk of this thing. Polestar itself calls the rear “UFO-esque,” and between the wraparound glass, the clamshell and the see-through floor, it’s a lot. But everything else on this car is pretty sharp.
Polestar is putting physical controls back in its cars and saying so in plain words. The way they talk about it makes it sound like you can expect that of upcoming production vehicles.
Now the usual caveat. A concept car doesn’t fix a balance sheet. Polestar lost $842 million in the first half of this year on a negative gross margin. Design has never been Polestar’s problem. Building these cars and selling them at a profit is.

title: CAT puts century-old train tech to work in its biggest underground machine yet
content:
Electric Heavy Machinery
Caterpillar
Jo Borrás
| Nov 10 2026 - 4:10 am PT
Diesel-electric locomotives have been barreling along America’s wide-open spaces for generations, and the century-old combination of highly efficient diesel engines spinning up generators to power high-torque electric motors has proven tough to beat. Now, Caterpillar is putting that century-old concept to work underground. Meet the CAT R3200 XE LHD.
One of the many hard-working machines moving chunks of Earth under your feet, an LHD (load, haul, and dump) machine is essentially a massive underground wheel loader designed to scoop up blasted rock, haul it through narrow mine tunnels,
then dump it into trucks or ore passes
. Built low and wide to fit in the tunnels, LHDs are workhorses of underground mining operations – and the new R3200 XE is CAT’s biggest yet, with a 25 ton payload and electric drive.
Before we get into the machine’s specs (the few that we have, anyway), I want to make sure understand that large-scale mining operations use obscene amounts of fuel, and a swing in site efficiency of just 1-2%
can mean a huge difference in the bottom line
– and fuel prices were up 27.4% (!)
in August alone
Keep the staggering weight of what that kind of fuel cost can mean to a fleet that buys fuel by the literal truckload as you read the rest of this.
Tier V CAT diesel
Via Caterpillar.
Though not yet officially released by CAT,
snippets of the company’s launch video have been leaking through dealers and trade journals
, and they show the big machine powered by CAT’s newest 18.1 liter Tier 5 C18 diesel generator making 527 hp (~390 kW). That C18 reportedly sends electrons to the same electric drive system used in the company’s already successful 18-ton R2900 XE LHD.
In addition to a bigger generator and heftier payload, CAT says the upcoming R3200 XE LHD offers reduced cycle times versus the R2900 XE with 11% better speed on grade, plus reduced maintenance and repair costs thanks to design refinements for better durability, including redesigned axle. All told, that works out to 28% more tons per hour with 8% better fuel efficiency.
That efficiency is boosted by the same baked-in ADAS tech that’s made the smaller R2900 XE a favorite, and includes the latest version of CAT AutoDig and MineStar, ensuring that the machines are easy for experienced CAT operators to set up for remote, semi-autonomous,
and even fully autonomous operation using Command for Underground
We’ll post an update once CAT makes the full rundown of official specs public, which should be sooner rather than later. When that happens, we’ll see exactly how this big burrowing CAT stacks up against the competition from
. In the meantime, let us know what you think of CAT’s newest electric drive machine in the comments.

title: Honda shows off its next electric motorcycle, and it’s wilder than you thought
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 10 2026 - 1:07 am PT
Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the company thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.
I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor. And that’s exactly the point.
The EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor. In fact, Honda
describes
the concept as looking toward the future of electric motorcycles beyond 2030.
The result is certainly unconventional.
This ain’t your
grandpa’s SuperCub
Instead of a centrally mounted motor driving the rear wheel, the EV Outlier uses motors inside both wheels, giving it all-wheel drive and allowing Honda’s designers to completely rethink the rest of the motorcycle’s layout. The battery is housed in that large central black body, while the rider sits extremely low and behind it.
Honda describes the design philosophy with three words: “Gliding, Ecstasy, and Low.” The first refers to the smooth, nearly silent feeling of electric propulsion, while the second describes the instant acceleration and massive torque available from independently controlled front and rear motors. “Low” is more literal: Honda deliberately dropped the rider’s seating and eye position to create an entirely different sensation from a conventional motorcycle.
There’s even a bucket-style backrest designed to support the rider under hard acceleration and let the rider pivot through corners around their hips.
Up front, traditional mirrors are replaced by cameras, while a wide digital cockpit can display things like lean angle, riding modes, front motor torque adjustment, and what the two wheels are doing in real time.
Will Honda actually build this thing? Almost certainly not exactly as you see it here. That’s what concepts are for.
But the EV Outlier is still interesting as a statement of intent. Honda is obviously still playing around with the freedom that electric drivetrains offer, and the company is asking what motorcycles could become once designers no longer have to work around engines, fuel tanks, transmissions, and traditional drivetrains.
And judging by what I saw at EICMA, Honda’s answer could get pretty wild.

title: Huaneng commissions dual-flywheel frequency regulation system, claims China single-unit power record - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
China’s Huaneng Group connected a 5.5 MW dual-flywheel energy storage system to the grid at its Lanzhou coal-fired power plant, enhancing frequency regulation capabilities. The system reportedly delivers sub-100-millisecond response times and over 99.5% accuracy, supporting grid stability amid growing renewable energy integration.
Vincent Shaw
10 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Energy Storage
Huaneng’s dual-flywheel frequency regulation system at Lanzhou plant
China-based Huaneng Group connected a dual-flywheel frequency regulation system to the grid at its Lanzhou combined heat and power plant on Nov. 6, completing a roughly year-long commissioning process that the group says validates large-scale flywheel storage for coal-fired generation assets.
The system comprises two flywheel units with a combined rating of 5.5 MW and 1.375 MWh. The primary unit — a 5 MW, 1.25 MWh flywheel spinning at up to 3,200 rpm on five-axis active magnetic levitation — is claimed by Huaneng to be the highest-power single flywheel unit in China. A secondary 0.5 MW, 125 kWh inertia flywheel handles smaller frequency deviations alongside it.
Huaneng says the paired design achieves a grid response time below 100 milliseconds and a regulation accuracy above 99.5%, figures the company attributes to the system’s proprietary control integration with the plant’s distributed control system. These performance figures have not been independently verified.
The pairing matters because flywheel storage is not designed for bulk energy delivery — 1.375 MWh is a small buffer — but for speed. Where a lithium battery frequency regulation system typically responds in a few hundred milliseconds, the flywheel array’s sub-100-millisecond response allows the thermal unit to react to grid disturbances faster than its own mechanical inertia would normally permit. The 5 MW primary flywheel handles large frequency excursions, while the smaller unit manages the finer, continuous corrections that would otherwise wear down the larger machine.
Technical development was led by the Xi’an Thermal Power Research Institute, Huaneng’s internal R&D arm, which has accumulated experience across several earlier thermal-storage combined frequency regulation demonstration projects. Equipment installation and the mandatory 168-hour continuous trial run were completed in December 2025; the system then operated under monitored conditions before the formal commercial grid connection this month.
The Lanzhou plant sits within Gansu province, a core zone of northwest China’s wind and solar buildout. Northwest China’s grids have faced persistent frequency stability challenges as variable renewable capacity has grown faster than conventional dispatchable generation. Thermal plants like the Lanzhou facility are under increasing pressure to act as regulating rather than baseload assets, and grid operators assess financial penalties under China’s two-part ancillary services assessment rules when frequency response falls short of benchmarks.
Huaneng’s stated rationale for the flywheel investment is partly to reduce those penalty costs while earning ancillary services revenue.
Flywheel storage carries structural advantages for this role — no chemical degradation, a claimed cycle life of tens of millions of charge-discharge cycles, and no fire risk — but remains more capital-intensive per megawatt than lithium battery alternatives at current prices.
Whether the dual-flywheel architecture proves economically replicable across other thermal plants will depend on how the ancillary services market values the importance of millisecond-range response.

title: Dual-oxide diffusion barrier boosts efficiency of mass-produced TOPCon solar cells by 0.07 percentage points - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Chinese researchers have developed a dual silicon oxide diffusion barrier strategy that improves phosphorus distribution and reduces contact resistance and optical losses in TOPCon solar cells. The industry-compatible process increased average cell efficiency from 27.15% to 27.22%, an absolute gain of 0.07 percentage points.
Emiliano Bellini
10 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Researchers at
Nanchang Hangkong University
in China have developed a dual silicon oxide (SiOₓ) diffusion barrier strategy to improve the efficiency of tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) solar cells. The approach combines post-plasma oxidation with tunnel oxide optimization to control the depth distribution of electrically active phosphorus and the microstructure of polysilicon (poly-Si).
“Conventional industrial TOPCon optimization mainly focuses on adjusting the total phosphorus dose or tunnel oxide quality, without independently controlling the position of the electrically active phosphorus peak within polysilicon,” corresponding author Wenhao Chen told
pv magazine.
“Phosphorus accumulation at the surface increases parasitic optical absorption without further reducing contact resistance, creating a trade-off between contact and optical losses in mass-produced cells.”
“Our work demonstrates an industry-compatible dual-SiOₓ diffusion barrier approach based on post-plasma oxidation,” Chen explained. “Rather than physically redistributing phosphorus atoms, inward-diffusing oxygen induces depth-selective dopant deactivation through the formation of electrically inactive P–O complexes. Extending post-plasma oxidation to 100 seconds shifts the activated phosphorus peak from the poly-Si surface to a depth of approximately 50 nm, closely matching the silver paste burn-off depth during screen-printing and co-firing.”
“Combined with a densified bottom tunnel oxide barrier, this dual-oxide confinement maintains high dopant activation and excellent passivation quality,” Chen said. “Industrial batch experiments involving nearly 1,000 TOPCon cells measuring 210 × 182.3 mm² demonstrate an absolute efficiency gain of 0.07 percentage points. The improvement mainly results from reduced contact resistivity and suppressed parasitic absorption, with only minor degradation in open-circuit voltage. This simple process modification can be implemented on existing PECVD production lines to further improve the efficiency of commercial TOPCon solar cells.”
The researchers fabricated TOPCon solar cells using n-type monocrystalline silicon wafers with resistivities ranging from 1 Ω cm to 3 Ω cm. The cells underwent conventional alkaline texturing, boron diffusion, rear-side TOPCon fabrication, passivation, screen printing, high-temperature co-firing and laser-enhanced contact optimization. A bilayer phosphorus-doped polysilicon structure incorporating silicon oxide diffusion barriers was deposited using plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) at approximately 435 C.
The team tested five post-plasma oxidation durations of 0, 66, 85, 100 and 120 seconds, with 66 seconds representing the conventional industrial process and 100 seconds the optimized condition. All samples subsequently underwent annealing at 910 C to crystallize the silicon layers and form the passivating contacts. The resulting polysilicon layer had a total thickness of approximately 100 nm.
The researchers used photoconductance measurements to assess passivation quality and the transmission line method to determine rear contact resistivity. Secondary ion mass spectrometry and electrochemical capacitance-voltage profiling were used to investigate elemental distributions and electrically active phosphorus concentrations. X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy provided further insights into crystallinity, surface morphology and chemical bonding. The finished cells underwent electrical performance testing to evaluate the effects of the different oxidation treatments.
The analysis showed that increasing oxidation time from the conventional 66 seconds to 100 seconds shifted the electrically active phosphorus peak from approximately 20 nm to 50 nm below the polysilicon surface. Further oxidation to 120 seconds caused excessive phosphorus deactivation and degraded passivation quality. By optimizing the bottom tunnel oxide barrier, the team maintained the phosphorus peak at around 50 nm while improving dopant activation and achieving an implied open-circuit voltage of 742.4 mV.
Material characterization suggested that inward-diffusing oxygen deactivates phosphorus through the formation of electrically inactive phosphorus-oxygen complexes rather than physically redistributing phosphorus atoms. The longer oxidation treatment also improved near-surface crystallinity and slightly increased surface roughness, while leaving overall polysilicon crystallinity largely unchanged. Contact resistivity decreased from 1.54 mΩ cm² to 1.00 mΩ cm², although the researchers could not attribute the improvement solely to the shift in the phosphorus peak.
Industrial testing involving 966 TOPCon cells showed that average conversion efficiency increased from 27.15% to 27.22%, representing a gain of 0.07 percentage points. The improvement was mainly driven by a higher fill factor and increased short-circuit current, while open-circuit voltage declined slightly. Quantum efficiency measurements indicated reduced parasitic absorption in the rear polysilicon contact, contributing to an improved long-wavelength response.
The researchers concluded that the optimized oxidation process offers a promising route to improving industrial TOPCon cell performance, although the individual contributions of dopant deactivation, structural changes and optical effects remain difficult to isolate.
The new process was described in “
Modulation of vertical activated phosphorus distribution via post-plasma oxidation and dual SiOx barrier in industrial TOPCon solar cells
,” published in
Solar Energy
. The research team included scientists from Chinese PV manufacturer ZQi Solar Technology.

title: Romania’s renewable project pipeline surpasses 114 GW - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Figures released by Romania’s energy regulator show 262 projects totaling 16.2 GW of approved export capacity had obtained connection contracts, building permits and establishment authorisations as of October 1.
Patrick Jowett
10 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Commercial & industrial
Energy Storage
Utility-scale
There are 1,625 renewable energy projects larger than 1 MW in Romania with valid grid connection permits, representing a total approved export capacity of 114.9 GW, according to figures published by the Romanian Energy Regulatory Authority (ANRE).
The figures, accurate as of October 1, show that 1,055 of these projects have also signed connection contracts, equivalent to 63.7 GW of approved export capacity.
A total of 749 projects, representing 41 GW, have also obtained building permits, while 262 projects, representing 16.2 GW of approved export capacity, have obtained ANRE establishment authorisations.
ANRE publishes figures on Romania’s renewable energy project pipeline on a monthly basis. Compared to figures from the start of September, the number of projects with valid grid connection permits has fallen by 1.1%, while the capacity of projects with all three major approvals has increased by 5.28%. This indicates that some projects are progressing through the development pipeline.
The regulator’s latest update also shows that 238 of the 749 renewable energy projects with both grid connection and building permits involve energy storage facilities or standalone storage installations. These projects represent more than 15.3 GW of approved maximum export capacity, just over 4 GW of which has a scheduled commissioning date in 2026.
ANRE’s update also includes a future commissioning schedule, with 259 projects representing 13.02 GW scheduled to come online in 2027. In total, 730 projects representing 40.4 GW have scheduled commissioning dates between 2026 and 2035.
Romania is one of Europe’s fastest growing solar markets in terms of newly-installed capacity. The country added
around 2.2 GW
of solar last year and is on course to deploy even more this year after cumulative solar capacity
exceeded 8.5 GW
If its current rate of solar deployment holds, Romania appears on track to reach its 2030 target of 10 GW of installed solar before the end of 2027. Its project pipeline includes the
largest planned solar project in the EU
, which reached financial close in September.

Research & Development
Japan’s state energy research agency says it is seeking renewable and energy storage options outside established areas such as solar that could suit regional conditions.
Brian Publicover
10 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Batteries
Commercial & industrial
Energy Storage
Hydrogen
Residential
Utility-scale
NEDO head office in Kawasaki, Japan
Japan’s New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) is commissioning a review of renewable energy and storage technologies that have reached the research or demonstration stage but never scaled, to inform its future R&D support.
NEDO has opened a call for a contractor to carry out the study, with a budget ceiling of JPY 20 million ($126,430) including tax – JPY 7 million in fiscal 2026 and JPY 13 million in fiscal 2027. Applications close at noon on Nov. 25, and the work runs to Oct. 31, 2027.
The survey covers electricity, heat, fuel, and energy storage technologies in Japan and overseas. It excludes in principle solar, wind, geothermal power and heat, and biomass, which NEDO said already receive sustained policy and R&D support, and excludes hydrogen, ammonia, nuclear, and fusion outright.
The contractor must compare the technologies it identifies on their technical features, R&D and commercialization trends, deployment potential, and barriers to commercialization, using quantitative indicators where possible, including patent filings and investment trends. It must also assess the regional conditions, uses, or markets under which each technology could be deployed, interview two or three experts, research institutes, or companies, and draw out implications for NEDO’s future R&D support. An interim report is due by the end of fiscal 2026 and a final report by Oct. 31, 2027.
NEDO said that alongside expanding major renewables, Japan needs R&D on technologies suited to each region’s natural, geographic, and social conditions to reach carbon neutrality by 2050. It plans to select the contractor in early December and publish the result on its website in mid-December.
NEDO set out a
solar technology strategy
in March 2025 and
R&D themes to expand solar adoption
in September 2025.
Under its Green Innovation Fund, NEDO opened calls for
tandem perovskite solar cell mass production
in October 2025 and
single-junction perovskite mass production
in May 2026. It also published
design and construction guidelines for flexible solar installations
in March 2026.

title: Swelect HHV secures ingot growers for 1 GW factory in India - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Raana Semiconductors will supply CZ12 silicon ingot growers to Swelect HHV Solar Photovoltaics for its 1 GW ingot and wafer manufacturing facility in India. The agreement also covers process optimization, recipe development and technical training.
Uma Gupta
10 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Raana Semiconductors has signed a preorder agreement with Swelect HHV Solar Photovoltaics, a wholly owned subsidiary of Swelect Energy Systems, to supply CZ12 silicon ingot growers. The equipment will be deployed at Swelect HHV’s 1 GW ingot and wafer manufacturing facility in India.
In addition to supplying the equipment, Raana Semiconductors will support Swelect HHV in process optimization and recipe development. Swelect HHV’s team will also receive training at Raana’s pilot facility to ensure efficient operation and maintenance of the equipment while minimizing downtime.
“Silicon ingot growth is the foundation of the solar value chain. Crystal quality, process stability, equipment uptime and yield at this first step carry through to wafer quality and cell efficiency downstream. They also determine factory utilization and whether the facility achieves its nameplate capacity,” said Raana Semiconductors. “By developing this capability in India using domestically manufactured equipment, we aim to strengthen local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.”
Swelect Energy Systems is an India-based solar manufacturer and energy solutions provider with operations spanning PV modules, power electronics, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), and energy storage.
The company expanded its PV module manufacturing capacity to more than 2 GW in September 2026
. Tamil Nadu-based Raana Semiconductors is developing domestically manufactured equipment for silicon crystal growth, with its CZ12 ingot growers targeting India’s emerging upstream PV manufacturing sector.
India is seeking to expand domestic ingot and wafer production to reduce its dependence on imports and address gaps in its solar manufacturing supply chain. The country, however, has made
limited progress in upstream manufacturing despite rapid expansion in module and cell production
. The government has extended its Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) framework to solar wafers, with mandatory compliance scheduled to begin on June 1, 2028. The policy requires wafer manufacturers to have equivalent ingot production capacity, while the initial approved list will depend on at least three independent wafer factories reaching a combined annual capacity of 15 GW.

title: Italian startup plans offshore gravity storage projects - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
Italian company Sizable Energy is developing a long-duration offshore energy storage system that uses deep-sea brine reservoirs to store electricity, with its first commercial projects planned for Calabria and Sicily and a demonstrator linked to a data center in Naples scheduled for 2027.
Sergio Matalucci
10 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Energy Storage
Sizable Energy is developing an offshore gravity-based energy storage system that uses seawater depths and high-density brine to store and return renewable electricity to the grid. The technology applies the principle of pumped hydro storage at sea, using flexible reservoirs on the seabed and at the surface instead of conventional water reservoirs at different elevations.
When surplus electricity is available, pumps move brine from a flexible reservoir on the seabed to a floating reservoir at the surface. When electricity is needed, the brine flows back down through a turbine to generate power. The company describes the system as a closed-loop design that uses commonly available materials, requires no lithium and consumes no land.
Sizable Energy co-founder Simone Biondi told
pv magazine Italia
that the company had completed its demonstration and concept-validation phase and moved into project development over the past year. It completed offshore tests in Reggio Calabria with the University of Reggio Calabria, following earlier tank testing at the Dutch marine research institute Marin. The tests validated key components under real conditions and demonstrated that deployment operations could be completed without specialized vessels.
The company has also received the European Commission’s STEP Seal and secured additional funding for an integrated demonstrator with a data center in Naples, scheduled for the first half of 2027. Pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) and front-end engineering design (FEED) activities are underway for an initial project in Calabria and a second in Sicily.
Biondi said Sizable Energy has built an international pipeline comprising more than 10 GWh of potential projects in the Mediterranean and Middle East, with advanced discussions also taking place in the Caribbean.
Ocean storage
Sizable Energy’s platform is designed to integrate with floating solar and offshore wind. Floating solar panels could share infrastructure, moorings and grid connection cables with the storage reservoirs. The company’s Power Shell concept also combines offshore storage, floating solar and data centers on a single platform.
Biondi said long-duration storage could shift solar generation from periods of high daytime production to evening and nighttime demand, while also helping cover longer periods of low renewable output. He identified data centers and other continuous loads as potential applications, particularly where renewable electricity supply is required around the clock.
The system separates power and energy capacity. Power output depends on water depth and the number of machines installed, while storage capacity depends on reservoir volume and depth. This allows the two parameters to be sized independently for different applications.
The company does not view lithium-ion battery energy storage systems (BESS) as direct competitors, but as complementary technologies. Biondi said its system could provide grid response, frequency services, reserves, balancing and physical or synthetic inertia, depending on its configuration.
He said the technology is particularly suited to utility-scale projects measured in gigawatt-hours (GWh), because storage costs scale with reservoir volume rather than the number of battery cells. Sizable Energy estimates a service life of more than 30 years, without cycle-related degradation, compared with the 10- to 15-year lifespan it attributes to conventional batteries.
Site requirements
The technology requires offshore sites with water depths of at least 500 meters and reasonable proximity to the coast and grid. Biondi said it is intended for utility-scale applications rather than smaller projects, where conventional battery systems remain more suitable.
He also acknowledged that the technology is at a first-of-a-kind stage. Although it uses components and materials already deployed in the offshore industry, integrating them into a new system architecture carries technical risks that must be addressed through field demonstrations.
In Italy, Biondi identified Terna’s Macse mechanism, which provides long-term contracts for storage capacity, as a potential framework for grid-connected projects. Sizable Energy is also exploring direct renewable power supply agreements with large consumers, including data centers, to secure long-term revenue.
Floating offshore wind is another potential application. Sizable Energy says its storage system could share export cables with offshore wind farms, allowing the connection to be sized closer to average rather than peak generation. Excess electricity could then be stored offshore and exported when cable capacity becomes available, reducing connection costs and curtailment.

content: Croatia’s Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition has launched a funding call to support renewable energy installations in the agricultural sector. The call is open to micro, small, medium and large-sized enterprises operating in agriculture. A total €30 million ($33.6 million) is available, with €20 million allocated to micro and small enterprises and €10 million to medium and large enterprises. Funding is provided through the Modernisation Fund. Applicants can apply for grants ranging from €5,000 to €5 million. Eligible investments include the construction or expansion of grid-connected solar power plants using modules with a minimum efficiency of 20%. Funding can also cover battery energy storage systems installed alongside a new or expanded solar plant, provided they are located behind the same metering point. Solar installations must be designed for self-consumption to be eligble, while battery storage systems must be designed to absorb at least 75% of the electricity generated by the directly-connected solar installation over the course of a year. Other eligible activities include design and construction supervision, occupational safety coordination during project implementation, and project management, including information and visibility activities. Further funding details published by the ministry explain the intensity of the grant varies depending on the size of the applicant and the type of investment. Micro and small enterprises can receive funding covering up to 65% of eligible solar PV costs and 50% of battery storage costs. The corresponding rates for medium-sized enterprises are 55% and 40%, while large enterprises can receive up to 45% for solar PV and 30% for battery storage. Applications can be submitted until Jan. 31, 2027, or until the available funding has been exhausted. Croatia’s cumulative solar capacity passed 1.2 GW by the start of December 2025. In March, the Croatian government announced plans to invest €40 million in household solar, batteries and heat pumps as part of its latest energy support measures. title: Price wars emerge as biggest challenge for Philippines solar installers - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
The main concerns facing solar installers in the Philippines are shifting from the warehouse to point of sale, with sales most likely to fall through either because customers are choosing the cheapest quote or because customers cannot pay upfront.
Patrick Jowett
10 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Research & Development
Asia-Pacific
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
Rooftops in Manila
Price wars currently stand as the biggest challenge facing solar installers in the Philippines, according to research by Manila-based nonprofit organisation New Energy Nexus (NEX) Philippines.
NEX Philippines first surveyed its network of rooftop solar installers in April to learn how the country’s oil and gas crisis was impacting businesses and recently conducted follow-up research to identify how solar adoption has since shifted.
The Philippines, which imports most of its oil from the Middle East, first declared an energy crisis in March following the start of the Strait of Hormuz crisis. It already had the costliest residential electricity prices in Southeast Asia at the time but prices have kept climbing since.
The start of the crisis brought increased interest in rooftop solar installations. Sheryl Estella, New Energy Skills Lead at NEX Philippines, told
pv magazine
that combined weekly installations among surveyed installers more than doubled after the energy emergency began, from around 30 systems a week to nearly 70.
While solar installers in the Philippines listed supply constraints as their leading concern in April, pricing wars and quality emerged as the leading concerns in September.
briefing paper
“Most installers convert a quarter or fewer of their inquiries,” the report says, adding that sales are now most likely to fall through either because customers are choosing the cheapest quote, or because customers cannot pay upfront.
Estella explained that price wars thrive because customers have no reliable way to tell a qualified installer from a cheap one, so they choose on price and overlook workmanship and after-sales service.  “As one installer told us: ‘Cheap alone is no longer enough. Serious clients want assurance that the system is reliable and that the company will still be there after installation’,” she said.
She added the Philippines would benefit from clearer standards for solar equipment and a practical accreditation pathway for installers that is supported by training and assessment, as well as a public list of certified products, in order to help customers make more informed decisions.
“These standards must be achievable for smaller installers, including those operating in provincial areas, so that professionalising the industry helps small businesses compete on quality and builds long-term trust in distributed solar, without making it harder for them to take part,” Estella said.
When asked by
pv magazine
what measures would best support Philippines’ installers and wider solar market, Estella pointed to finance first.
“Installers lose sales when customers cannot pay upfront, and the Social Security System’s planned solar loans would reach further if members could apply through their installer at the point of sale,” she added.
Estella also looked to permitting as another way to support installers. While the government of the Philippines has
moved to shorten permitting times
since the beginning of the energy crisis, Estella explained that it currently publishes no data on whether those deadlines are met and sets no penalties when they are missed.
“Compliance data, a plain-language guide for installers and consequences for missed deadlines would turn the new rules into faster connections,” she said.
While supply constraints no longer stand as the greatest concern among solar installers in the Philippines, the report says these constraints have eased rather than been solved, with lead times still sometimes costing deals. It also notes that while demand has moved past a panic buying stage, interest in rooftop solar still remains considerably above the level recorded before the start of the energy crisis.
The Philippines is currently considered one of the world’s leading import hubs from solar panels having
imported 4 GW
of Chinese solar panels over the first four months of this year. As of July, a
further 3 GW
were heading to the country.

title: DMEGC launches steel-framed solar module series - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The new series of n-type bifacial solar modules features a steel frame with an S-shaped cross-section. The modules deliver 640 W to 665 W of power output and offer a bifaciality factor of up to 85%, with the new frame design reportedly reducing rear-side shading by 76%.
Emiliano Bellini
10 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Utility-scale
The DMxxxG12RT-B66HSW 640~665W module
Chinese solar manufacturer
has unveiled a new series of bifacial glass-glass photovoltaic modules featuring a steel frame designed to improve mechanical reliability and rear-side power generation.
“The zinc-aluminum-magnesium (Zn-Al-Mg) coated steel used in the frames has nearly twice the tensile strength of conventional aluminum alloys, enabling the modules to withstand snow loads of up to 6,000 Pa and wind loads of up to 5,000 Pa when installed with suitable mounting systems,” a spokesperson from the company told
pv magazine
DMEGC said the material also has a lower coefficient of thermal expansion, compared with aluminum and glass. The closer thermal expansion characteristics of steel and glass could reduce mechanical stress and the risk of cell microcracks during temperature fluctuations, the company said.
The frame features an S-shaped cross-section that reportedly reduces vertical shading on the rear side of the module by 76% compared with conventional frame designs. DMEGC said the geometry increases the unshaded rear-side area by 3.6%, resulting in a theoretical improvement in bifaciality of approximately 2.8%.
The new Infinity RT 3.0 series comprises six models with power outputs ranging from 640 W to 665 W and efficiencies between 23.7% and 24.6%.
The DMxxxG12RT-B66HSW 640~665W modules are based on 132 n-type monocrystalline half-cut cells and measure 2,382 mm × 1,134 mm × 30 mm, with a weight of 33.3 kg. They feature 2 mm heat-strengthened glass on both sides and are designed for utility-scale PV applications.
The modules achieve a bifaciality factor of up to 85%, according to the manufacturer. DMEGC’s energy yield simulations indicate annual electricity generation of 2,078 kWh/kWp, corresponding to a 0.6% increase in generation revenue compared with conventional modules under the simulated conditions.
The modules feature a maximum system voltage of 1,500 V and an operating temperature range of -40 C to 85 C. Their temperature coefficient is -0.28%/C, while the nominal module operating temperature is 42 C.
DMEGC said the products have undergone salt mist and ammonia corrosion testing, as well as extended stress testing.
The manufacturer offers a 15-year product warranty and a 30-year linear power output warranty. It guarantees no more than 1% degradation in the first year and a maximum annual degradation rate of 0.35% thereafter, with a guaranteed power output of 88.85% after 30 years.

title: Chilong-1: China starts building 600-MW reactor at hybrid nuclear site
content: Workers have poured the first concrete for the nuclear island at the Xuwei plant in Jiangsu province. The milestone marks the official start of construction on the world’s first commercial “Chilong-1” reactor. The project sets a precedent for using nuclear energy to power large-scale chemical manufacturing.Unlike conventional nuclear sites built almost exclusively for the electrical grid, the Xuwei complex will function primarily as an industrial steam supplier. It provides heat directly to nearby petrochemical refineries while sending surplus electricity to the regional network. Once fully operational, its first phase will provide 32.5 million tonnes of industrial steam each year and generate over 11.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity. Replacing fossil fuels here will cut standard coal use by 7.26 million tonnes each year. According to official estimates, this will prevent nearly 19.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions.The plant achieves this output through an unusual hybrid design. It will pair two distinct nuclear technologies on a single site. These nuclear technologies are “Hualong One” pressurized water reactors and the “Chilong-1” high-temperature gas-cooled reactor. Using a coordinated control architectureThe system runs in sequence to produce steam with exact thermodynamic properties. Main steam from the third-generation Hualong One first turns demineralized water into saturated steam. The fourth-generation Chilong-1 then takes that steam and superheats it further, yielding three separate grades of high-temperature steam tailored for petrochemical refining.To manage this tandem operation safely, plant operators will use a unified “reactor-machine-heat” coordinated control architecture. It is the first time a commercial facility has run both reactor types under a single integrated heat-delivery framework.Jointly developed by China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) and Tsinghua University, the Chilong-1 relies on fourth-generation nuclear principles that emphasize passive safety. The reactor is designed to remain safe during severe system failures without requiring active operator intervention or external power supplies. Even under complete coolant loss, the physics of the core prevents a meltdown and blocks large releases of radioactive material.A modular layoutThe reactor also uses a modular layout. Individual units produce relatively modest amounts of power on their own, but engineers can link multiple modules together depending on regional energy needs. Beyond supplying industrial process heat, the high temperatures produced by the core make the reactor well suited for large-scale hydrogen production and efficient electrical generation.China Nuclear Power Investment, a subsidiary of CNNC, manages the Xuwei site. The first phase includes two Hualong One reactors alongside the single Chilong-1 unit. Work on the first Hualong One began on 16 January. “It opens a new chapter in providing a replicable and scalable “Chinese solution” for the low-carbon transformation of high-energy-consuming industries worldwide, injecting strong momentum into the realization of global carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals,” the Global Times reported at the time.When completed, the plant will serve as a permanent low-carbon heat and power anchor for the Lianyungang petrochemical industrial base.
